chunks: And from him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from Jaʿfar ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān, from Idrīs ibn ʿAbdillāh al-Qummī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who is praying while opposite him there is a woman standing in janabah upon her bedding. He said: “If she is sitting, it does not harm you; but if she is praying, then no.”

key_terms.تَضُرُّكَ: harms you, meaning negatively affects your prayer
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: in a state of janabah, requiring ghusl

ai.seo_question: Does a woman in janabah sitting or praying opposite a man affect his salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a man praying while a woman in a state of janabah is positioned opposite him. It indicates that if she is sitting, it does not affect his prayer, but if she is herself praying opposite him, then that is not permitted.
